title: The heat that cannot leave
question: How do human activities warm the whole planet, and what follows?
hook: The gases from a car's tailpipe and a power plant's chimney end up changing sea levels for centuries.
idea: Greenhouse gases from fossil fuels trap some of Earth's outgoing heat, driving warming whose effects outlast any cuts.

beats.prompt: Sunlight warms the ground, and the ground then gives off heat. The air now holds about 50% more carbon dioxide than before industry. What happens to that outgoing heat?

choices.label: Some of it is absorbed by the gases, warming the lower air
It escapes to space faster than before
choices.feedback: Extra greenhouse gas does the opposite: it absorbs some of the heat on its way out.

choices.label: It is reflected back toward the Sun by the gas
choices.feedback: The gases absorb outgoing heat; they do not bounce it back to the Sun.

choices.label: Nothing changes, since carbon dioxide is a small share of air
choices.feedback: Carbon dioxide is the main gas driving global warming despite being a small share of the air.

beats.explain: Greenhouse gases absorb some of the heat the Earth radiates after sunlight warms it, which warms the lower atmosphere.

beats.prompt: Put these moments in Earth's climate story in order, from oldest to newest.
items: Last Interglacial, seas 5 to 10 metres higher
2024 becomes the warmest year on record
beats.explain: The Last Interglacial was about 125,000 years ago, the glacial maximum 20,000 years ago, the current stable period began 11,700 years ago, and 2024 set the record.

beats.prompt: Sort each into what drives warming and what helps cut it.
items: Switching to wind and solar power
Farming that stores carbon in soil
beats.explain: Fossil fuel use, deforestation and some farming and industry release greenhouse gases; clean energy, more forest and soil-storing farming cut or remove carbon.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: Nations agreed in Paris to keep warming well under 2 °C.
Countries then made pledges under the Agreement.
Those pledges are enough to meet the Paris goal.
So no further cuts would be needed this century.
beats.explain: With the pledges made under the Agreement, warming would still reach about 2.8 °C by century's end, well above the goal.
